segments.title: Groundwork for the new components and composables
context: This change adds a Pokemon page at /pokemon and a link to it in the header of every page, and installs Pinia in the app. The page lists the Pokemon from the API with their level and types, and a professor can narrow the list to one type or to the Pokemon of one trainer.

waypoints.title: Added `formatTypes()` to write the types of a Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author added a function `formatTypes()` that returns the primary type of a Pokemon, or both types joined by ` / ` when it has a second type, such as `water / flying`. [`PokemonPage` calls it for each Pokemon of the list](code:src/views/pokemon/PokemonPage.vue#L16), so that each line shows the types after the name and the level.

waypoints.title: Added the Pinia store of the Pokemon filters
waypoints.reading:
The author added a Pinia setup store `usePokemonFiltersStore` that:

- keeps the chosen type in `type` and the chosen trainer in `trainerId`, both `null` at first
- sets both back to `null` with `clear()`

[`PokemonFilters` binds its selects to the two refs](code:src/views/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.vue#L8-9) and [`usePokemon()` reads them](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#L14), with no import between the two, so that a pick in the filters changes the list the page shows.
waypoints.coreChange: This store is where the filters live. The selects of the filter component write it and [`usePokemon()`](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#usePokemon) reads it, so what each filter starts at and what `clear()` sets decide what the page lists.

findings.title: `usePokemonFiltersStore` keeps the filters after the page closes
findings.reading: [`defineStore()` makes one store for the whole app](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L5), and [`createPinia()` installs it on the app](code:src/main.ts#L11), outside every page. So the chosen type and trainer stay set when a professor opens another page and comes back to /pokemon. Should the page open with the filters the professor chose last, or with no filter?

waypoints.title: Added the list of Pokemon types
waypoints.reading: The author added a constant `POKEMON_TYPES` that lists the 18 Pokemon types, from `"normal"` to `"fairy"`. [`PokemonFilters` renders one option per type](code:src/views/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.vue#L17), so that the type filter offers every type.

waypoints.title: Added the type of one Pokemon type
waypoints.reading: The author added a type `PokemonType` that is the union of the names in `POKEMON_TYPES`. [The filter store keeps the chosen type as one](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L6), so that the store holds only a type the list has.

waypoints.title: Added the `Pokemon` interface
waypoints.reading: The author added an interface `Pokemon` with an `id`, a `name`, a `level`, a `primary_type`, a `secondary_type` that is `null` for a Pokemon with one type, and a `trainer_id` that is `null` for a Pokemon with no trainer. The fields keep the snake_case names of the JSON the API returns, so that [`fetchPokemon()`](code:src/api/pokemon.ts#fetchPokemon) returns the response as it is.

waypoints.title: Modified `RootLayout` to link to the Pokemon page
waypoints.reading: The author modified the component `RootLayout` to render a `<RouterLink to="/pokemon">` with the text `Pokemon` in the header, between `Trainers` and `Items`. [The router renders `PokemonPage` at that path](code:src/router.ts#L16), so that a professor can open the new page from every page.

waypoints.title: Added `fetchPokemon()` to request the Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author added a function `fetchPokemon()` that sends a `GET` request to `/pokemon`, with `?trainer_id=` and the id when a trainer is chosen, and returns the Pokemon of the response. [`request()` puts `/api` in front of the path](code:src/api/client.ts#L10). [`usePokemon()` runs `fetchPokemon()` as its query function](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#L17), so that the page loads only the Pokemon of the chosen trainer.

waypoints.title: Added the query key of the Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author added a constant `POKEMON_QUERY_KEY` that holds `"pokemon"`. [`usePokemon()` puts it in a key with the ref of the chosen trainer](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#L16), so that each trainer has its own cached list and a new trainer loads the list again.

waypoints.title: Added `hasType()` to match a Pokemon against the type filter
waypoints.reading: The author added a function `hasType()` that returns `true` when no type is chosen, or when the primary or the secondary type of the Pokemon is the chosen type. [The computed list of `usePokemon()` calls it](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#L19), so that a Pokemon with two types shows under both of them.

waypoints.title: Added `usePokemon()` to load the Pokemon that match the filters
waypoints.reading:
The author added a composable `usePokemon()` that:

- reads the chosen type and trainer from [the filter store](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFiltersStore) as refs
- loads the Pokemon of the trainer with [`fetchPokemon()`](code:src/api/pokemon.ts#fetchPokemon), under a key that holds the trainer
- keeps the Pokemon of the chosen type in a computed `pokemon`, with [`hasType()`](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#hasType)
- returns the query with `pokemon` added

[`PokemonPage` calls it](code:src/views/pokemon/PokemonPage.vue#L6), so that the list follows both filters. The trainer filter goes to the API, and the type filter runs in the browser on the loaded list.
waypoints.coreChange: This is where the two filters reach the data: the trainer goes into the query key and the request, and the type filters the loaded list in a computed. The page, the filter component and the store all exist for it.

children.title: Added the refs of the two filters
children.reading: The author added a call to `storeToRefs()` on [the filter store](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFiltersStore), which returns `type` and `trainerId` as refs. [The query key holds `trainerId`](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#L16), and [the computed list reads `type`](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#L19), so that both follow the selects.

children.title: Added the query of the Pokemon
children.reading: The author added a call to `useQuery` with the key `["pokemon", trainerId]` and a query function that calls [`fetchPokemon(trainerId.value)`](code:src/api/pokemon.ts#fetchPokemon). Vue Query watches the ref in the key, so a new trainer requests the list again.

findings.title: `usePokemon()` empties the list each time the trainer changes
findings.reading: [The query key holds `trainerId`](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#L16), so a new trainer starts a new query with no data. While it loads, `isPending` is `true`, so [the page shows `Loading the Pokemon…` in place of the list](code:src/views/pokemon/PokemonPage.vue#L13). `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` from `@tanstack/vue-query` keeps the last list on screen until the new one arrives, for one more option. The fix also imports `keepPreviousData` on [the first line of the file](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#L1).

children.title: Added the computed list of the chosen type
children.reading: The author added a `computed` that takes the loaded Pokemon, or `[]` before they load, and keeps those for which [`hasType()`](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#hasType) returns `true` with the chosen type. A new type only runs the computed again on the cached list, with no request.

children.title: Added the return of the query and the list
children.reading: The author added a return of every field of the query with `pokemon` beside them. [`PokemonPage` reads `pokemon`, `isPending` and `isError` from it](code:src/views/pokemon/PokemonPage.vue#L6).

waypoints.title: Added Pinia to the app
waypoints.reading: The author added a call to `app.use(createPinia())` that installs Pinia on the app before Vue Query. [`usePokemonFiltersStore()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFiltersStore) needs an installed Pinia, so that [`PokemonFilters`](code:src/views/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.vue#L8) and [`usePokemon()`](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#L14) get the same store.

waypoints.title: Modified the router to add the Pokemon page
waypoints.reading: The author modified the router `router` to add a child route `pokemon` of the layout that renders [`PokemonPage`](code:src/views/pokemon/PokemonPage.vue#PokemonPage). [`src/main.ts` installs the router](code:src/main.ts#L10), so that the page opens at `/pokemon` inside [`RootLayout`](code:src/views/RootLayout.vue#RootLayout), where [the header links to it](code:src/views/RootLayout.vue#L14).

waypoints.title: Added `PokemonPage` to list the Pokemon
waypoints.reading:
The author added a page component `PokemonPage` that:

- renders the heading `Pokemon` and [`PokemonFilters`](code:src/views/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.vue#PokemonFilters)
- loads the Pokemon that match the filters with [`usePokemon()`](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#usePokemon)
- shows `Loading the Pokemon…` while they load, and `The Pokemon could not be loaded.` when the request fails
- renders one line per Pokemon with its name, its level and [its types](code:src/lib/format.ts#formatTypes)

[The router renders it at `/pokemon`](code:src/router.ts#L16), and [the header links to it](code:src/views/RootLayout.vue#L14), so that a professor can browse the Pokemon.

children.title: Added the query of the Pokemon
children.reading: The author added a call to [`usePokemon()`](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#usePokemon) that gives the filtered `pokemon` and the flags `isPending` and `isError`. [The three conditions of the template read them](code:src/views/pokemon/PokemonPage.vue#L13-15).

children.reading:
The author added a `v-if` that renders `

Loading the Pokemon…

` while the query is pending. [The filters stay above it](code:src/views/pokemon/PokemonPage.vue#L12), so a professor can change them while the list loads.

children.title: Added the error message of the Pokemon list
children.reading:
The author added a `v-else-if` that renders `

The Pokemon could not be loaded.

` when the query fails, as it does when [`request()` throws an `ApiError`](code:src/api/client.ts#L14).

children.title: Added the list of the Pokemon
children.reading: The author added a `v-else` that renders a `<ul>` with one `<li>` per Pokemon that shows its name, `Lv.` and its level, and the text of [`formatTypes()`](code:src/lib/format.ts#formatTypes).

findings.title: `PokemonPage` renders an empty list when no Pokemon matches
findings.reading: When the trainer has no Pokemon, or none of them has the chosen type, [the computed `pokemon` is `[]`](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#L19). The `v-else` then renders an empty `<ul>`, and the professor sees the filters with nothing under them. A message for an empty list says that the filters match nothing, for one more condition.

waypoints.title: Added `PokemonFilters` to choose the filters
waypoints.reading:
The author added a component `PokemonFilters` that:

- renders a select with `Every type` and one option per type of [`POKEMON_TYPES`](code:src/types/pokemon.ts#POKEMON_TYPES)
- renders a select with `Every trainer` and one option per trainer from [`useTrainers()`](code:src/composables/use-trainers.ts#L6-8)
- binds each select to its filter of the store with `v-model`
- renders a `Clear filters` button that clears both filters

[`PokemonPage` renders it above the list](code:src/views/pokemon/PokemonPage.vue#L12), so that a professor can narrow the list.

children.title: Added the read of the filter store
children.reading: The author added a call to [`usePokemonFiltersStore()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFiltersStore) that returns the store. [The Clear filters button calls `clear()` on it](code:src/views/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.vue#L23).

children.title: Added the refs of the two filters
children.reading: The author added a call to `storeToRefs()` that returns `type` and `trainerId` as refs of the store. [The type select binds `type` with `v-model`](code:src/views/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.vue#L15) and [the trainer select binds `trainerId`](code:src/views/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.vue#L19), so a pick writes the store with no handler.

children.title: Added the query of the trainers
children.reading: The author added a call to [`useTrainers()`](code:src/composables/use-trainers.ts#L6-8) that gives the loaded trainers, `undefined` until they arrive. [The trainer select renders one option per trainer](code:src/views/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.vue#L21), so the select offers only `Every trainer` while the trainers load.

findings.title: `PokemonFilters` hides a failed load of the trainers
findings.reading: [`useTrainers()` reports a failed request in `isError`](code:src/composables/use-trainers.ts#L7), and `PokemonFilters` reads only `data`. So when the trainers do not load, [the trainer select offers `Every trainer` alone](code:src/views/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.vue#L19-22), and nothing tells the professor why. The fix reads `isError` here, and the trainer select then needs a message for it.
trace: [The trainer select renders `Every trainer` and no other option](code:src/views/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.vue#L19-22).
findings.solution: const { data: trainers, isError: hasTrainerError } = useTrainers()

children.title: Added one option per Pokemon type
children.reading: The author added a `v-for` that renders one `<option>` per name of [`POKEMON_TYPES`](code:src/types/pokemon.ts#POKEMON_TYPES), with the name as its value and as its text.

children.title: Added one option per trainer
children.reading: The author added a `v-for` that renders one `<option>` per trainer, with the `id` as its value and the `name` as its text. [`v-model` writes the number to `trainerId`](code:src/views/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.vue#L19), and [`usePokemon()` puts it in its query key](code:src/composables/use-pokemon.ts#L16).

children.title: Added the button that clears the filters
children.reading: The author added a `<BaseButton variant="ghost">` with the text `Clear filters` that calls [`clear()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L9-12) on the store when clicked. Both selects show their `Every` option again, and the page lists every Pokemon.
